nodes.name: Poll Schedule (Every 5 Min)
nodes.notes: The cycle. The interval is a node setting (n8n does not allow expressions here), so change it on this node if you want a different cadence.

nodes.name: Manual Check Webhook
nodes.notes: POST {force?: true}. Runs one cycle now and returns the digest. force=true pushes through even if another cycle holds the lock.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { triggered_by: 'schedule', force: false, headers: {} } }];

assignments.name: TRANSIENT_PATTERNS_JSON
assignments.value: ["time-?d? ?out", "econnreset", "econnrefused", "enotfound", "eai_again", "etimedout", "socket hang up", "closed unexpectedly", "perhaps it is offline", "rate limit", "too many requests", "service unavailable", "bad gateway", "gateway time-?out", "temporar"]

assignments.name: PERMANENT_PATTERNS_JSON
assignments.value: ["unauthori[sz]ed", "forbidden", "invalid credentials", "authorization failed", "bad request", "not found", "could not be found", "unprocessable", "validation", "invalid (input|parameter|value)", "credentials? (not|are not) (set|found)"]

nodes.name: CONFIG
nodes.notes: THE ONLY NODE YOU NEED TO EDIT. n8n API address and key, state-service address, Slack, thresholds, backoff, patterns. See the Read Me First note and the README.

nodes.name: Monitor Rules
nodes.notes: EDIT ME for what is special about your workflows: ignore some, retry others less or never, never retry risky nodes, and the wording of the alert. Data only; checked every cycle. The lock, window, backoff, storm and cooldown logic cannot be changed here.

nodes.name: Validate Trigger
nodes.notes: Auth token (manual calls only) and CONFIG sanity. A broken config says what is wrong instead of failing mysteriously later.

nodes.name: Fail Scheduled Run (Misconfigured)
nodes.notes: A scheduled run with a broken config fails loudly (visible in the Executions list and to n8n's own Error Workflow) rather than silently doing nothing.

nodes.name: Respond JSON
nodes.notes: Every manual-run answer (rejections, skips, degraded, digest) goes through this node.

nodes.name: Acquire Poll Lock
nodes.notes: Atomic, self-expiring lock: only one cycle runs at a time, and a crashed cycle cannot deadlock future ones (the TTL expires). Returns {acquired, token}.

nodes.name: Evaluate Lock
nodes.notes: Distinguishes three outcomes: got the lock, another cycle holds it (skip), or the state service itself is down (degraded, NOT mistaken for "busy").

nodes.name: Get Last Checked Timestamp
nodes.notes: The watermark: where the last fully completed cycle stopped. 404 or null = first run.

nodes.name: Compute Poll Window
nodes.notes: since = watermark (or a bootstrap lookback on the first run), until = when this cycle started. Window is [since, until).

nodes.name: Fetch Failed Executions Page
nodes.notes: n8n public API: newest first, cursor pagination. The API has no "since" filter, so the time window is applied in the next node.

nodes.name: Accumulate Page
nodes.notes: Collects every page fetched so far (by reading all runs of the fetch node), applies the time window, and drops executions that were already retried successfully, are manual test runs, or belong to the monitor itself.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { cursor: $json.next_cursor } }];

nodes.name: Assess Failure Batch
nodes.notes: Storm check: STORM_THRESHOLD or more distinct workflows failing in one window = probably one shared outage.

nodes.name: Get Storm Alert State
nodes.notes: Storm alerts have their own cooldown (kept as a pseudo-incident) so a long outage is one page, not one every cycle.

nodes.name: Split Into Per-Execution Items
nodes.notes: Newest first, capped at MAX_EXECUTIONS_PER_CYCLE so one bad hour cannot trigger hundreds of detail calls.

nodes.name: Classify Failure
nodes.notes: transient (5xx, 429, timeouts, resets: worth retrying) / permanent (other 4xx, auth, validation: a person must fix it) / unknown (never auto-retried). HTTP status is checked first, then your regex lists from CONFIG.

nodes.name: Group Into Incidents
nodes.notes: One incident = workflow + failed node + failure type (NOT the execution id: every retry gets a new one). Ten failed runs of the same bug become ONE incident with ten executions, so retries and pages are counted per incident.

nodes.name: Get Workflow
nodes.notes: One call per incident (not per execution): is the workflow still active, and what is it called?

nodes.name: Evaluate Workflow
nodes.notes: Skips workflows that are switched off (someone is probably fixing them) or deleted.

nodes.name: Get Incident State
nodes.notes: Retry count, next allowed retry time and last-alert time for this incident. 404 = never seen before.

nodes.name: Decide Action
nodes.notes: Only transient failures are retried. Permanent and unknown go straight to a person. Retries exhausted escalates. Inside a backoff window it waits. During a storm it suppresses.

nodes.name: Expand To Executions
nodes.notes: Each failed execution in the incident is retried (up to MAX_RETRIES_PER_INCIDENT_PER_CYCLE), but the incident is charged ONE attempt for the cycle.

nodes.name: Retry Execution
nodes.notes: POST /executions/{id}/retry (needs the execution:retry API-key scope).

nodes.name: Evaluate Retry Dispatch
nodes.notes: Back to one item per incident: did at least one retry dispatch?

nodes.name: Compute Backoff
nodes.notes: Exponential backoff with jitter: 5m, 15m, 45m by default.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { workflow_id: $json.workflow_id, workflow_name: $json.workflow_name, failed_node: $json.failed_node, failure_type: $json.failure_type, error_message: $json.error_message, last_failure_at: $json.last_failure_at, last_seen_at: Date.now(), status: 'open', phase: 'retrying', retries_used: $json.retries_used, next_retry_at: $json.next_retry_at, ...($json.is_new_incident ? { opened_at: Date.now() } : {}) } }}

nodes.name: Write Retry State
nodes.notes: Records everything the recovery check later needs (workflow id, failed node, last failure time), not just the counters.

nodes.name: In Alert Cooldown?
nodes.notes: One page per incident per ALERT_COOLDOWN_MINUTES (30 by default), not one per poll cycle.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { workflow_id: $json.workflow_id, workflow_name: $json.workflow_name, failed_node: $json.failed_node, failure_type: $json.failure_type, error_message: $json.error_message, last_failure_at: $json.last_failure_at, last_seen_at: Date.now(), status: 'open' } }}

nodes.name: Evaluate Alert Result
nodes.notes: If Slack rejects the post, the cooldown is NOT started, so the next cycle pages again instead of the alert silently vanishing.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { workflow_id: $json.workflow_id, workflow_name: $json.workflow_name, failed_node: $json.failed_node, failure_type: $json.failure_type, error_message: $json.error_message, last_failure_at: $json.last_failure_at, last_seen_at: Date.now(), status: 'open', phase: 'escalated', escalated: true, escalate_reason: $json.escalate_reason, ...($json.record_alerted ? { last_alerted_at: Date.now() } : {}), ...($json.is_new_incident ? { opened_at: Date.now() } : {}) } }}

parameters.jsCode: return $input.all().map((it) => ({ json: { incident_key: it.json.incident_key, workflow_id: it.json.workflow_id, outcome: 'waiting_backoff', retries_used: it.json.retries_used, next_retry_at: it.json.next_retry_at } }));
return $input.all().map((it) => ({ json: { incident_key: it.json.incident_key, workflow_id: it.json.workflow_id, outcome: 'suppressed_storm' } }));
return $input.all().map((it) => ({ json: { incident_key: it.json.incident_key, workflow_id: it.json.workflow_id, outcome: 'state_error' } }));

nodes.name: Outcome: State Error
nodes.notes: The state service could not be read for this incident, so nothing was done for it. The watermark is NOT advanced, so the next cycle looks at the same window again.

parameters.jsCode: return $input.all().map((it) => ({ json: { incident_key: it.json.incident_key, workflow_id: it.json.workflow_id, outcome: 'skipped', reason: it.json.skip_reason } }));

nodes.name: Merge Outcomes
nodes.notes: Branches that converge must go through a Merge: a plain Code node with several inputs runs once PER ARRIVAL (this is how the original ran its summary several times).

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { outcome: 'none' } }];

nodes.name: Get Open Incidents
nodes.notes: Recovery runs every cycle, after the failure lane, whether or not this cycle found new failures: a workflow can heal between polls.

parameters.jsCode: return $input.first().json.candidates.map((c) => ({ json: c }));

nodes.name: Check Recent Success
nodes.notes: Newest successful run of the workflow. The workflow must save successful executions (n8n default) for this to work.

nodes.name: Evaluate Recovery
nodes.notes: Recovered = the workflow has a successful run that started AFTER the incident's last recorded failure.

nodes.name: Build Recovery Message
nodes.notes: Resolves first, announces second: never say "recovered" for an incident that could not be closed.

parameters.jsCode: return $input.all().map((it) => ({ json: { incident_key: it.json.incident_key, workflow_id: it.json.workflow_id, outcome: it.json.check_ok ? 'still_open' : 'recovery_check_failed' } }));
return [{ json: { outcome: 'none', recovery_ok: $('Prepare Recovery Checks').first().json.recovery_ok } }];

nodes.name: Build Completed Outcome
nodes.notes: Digest. The watermark advances ONLY if nothing was skipped or lost this cycle.

nodes.name: Build Degraded Outcome
nodes.notes: The monitor monitoring itself: an unreachable n8n API or state service is its own loud failure, never "zero failures this cycle". Alerts are rate-limited per reason so an outage does not page every five minutes.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: $input.first().json }];

nodes.name: Cycle Outcome
nodes.notes: Every way a cycle can end lands here, then runs the same tail: alert, watermark, release the lock, respond.

nodes.name: Record Cycle Alert
nodes.notes: Monitor-level alerts (degraded, completed with warnings) are rate-limited per reason using the workflow's own static data, because the state service may be the very thing that is down.

nodes.name: Release Poll Lock
nodes.notes: Releases only the lock THIS cycle holds (token). A forced-through manual run holds no token, so it can never release another cycle's lock.

parameters.jsCode:
const o = $('Cycle Outcome').first().json;
return [{ json: { triggered_by: o.triggered_by, http_status: o.http_status, response_body: o.response_body } }];

parameters.content:
## Self-Healing Execution Monitor
**Setup (about 10 minutes)**
1. In n8n: Settings > n8n API > create a key with scopes `workflow:read`, `workflow:list`, `execution:read`, `execution:list`, `execution:retry`.
2. Run a state service (a reference one is included: `node 10-self-healing-execution-monitor-mock-server.js`, port 4200).
3. Open **CONFIG**: set `N8N_API_URL` (e.g. `http://localhost:5678/api/v1`), `N8N_API_KEY`, `MONITOR_STATE_API_URL`, and optionally `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`.
4. Activate. It runs every 5 minutes, or POST `/webhook/monitor/check-now` to run one cycle now.

**Each cycle:** lock -> window -> failed executions -> group into incidents -> retry transient / escalate the rest -> recovery check -> digest -> advance watermark (only if nothing was lost) -> unlock.

Monitored workflows must save failed AND successful executions (n8n default).
